column1: # A3.3's opening map: the camera subsystem, bounded before anything is read.
# THE FIRST THING TO SAY IS THAT IT IS NAMED. Every class in the flight thread
# was among the 306 vtables without RTTI; cycle 1385 called finding ONE named
# class -- CX360UnitManager -- the thread's first anchor. The camera subsystem
# AND THE SECOND IS THAT IT IS NOT VIRTUAL-DISPATCH DRIVEN. Measured, not
# assumed: each of the three core vtables holds exactly ONE slot.
# One slot is a destructor. So these are DATA classes, and the per-frame camera
# work is in plain functions that operate on them -- the exact opposite of the
# flight model, where every behaviour was a vtable slot of an unnamed class and
# the whole difficulty was finding which slot ran.
# A3.3 therefore inverts A3.2's method. There is no "who calls slot N" to run.
# The handle is instead: WHO BUILDS A CGaCamera. The vtable is materialised at

# TWO CANDIDATES FOR THE GAMEPLAY CAMERA, on position rather than on name:
#   0x82300C20 -- 1,985 instructions, 422 of them vector, ONE caller, and it
#   sits at 0x8230xxxx, inside the same span as the flight model's slot 30
#   (0x82303E68) and its step (0x82306A38). Size and neighbourhood both fit a
#   per-frame camera that follows the aeroplane.
#   0x82212868 / 0x82212BD8 -- small, five and two callers, at 0x8221xxxx,
#   which is where the contracted input consumer 0x82211C10 lives.
# NEITHER IS ESTABLISHED. Position in the image is not evidence -- cycle 1379's
# twenty-fourth shape is exactly that, and the refuted-link shape before it.
# What IS established is the population: 27 functions, sized, with their caller
# counts, and a named class to anchor them to.
